chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Lecture-demonstrations at the University of Virginia on the saxophone
summary: Invited by George Starks he gave a lecture on saxophone history from Hawkins to Coltrane, whose tune Big Nick drew students to him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You did some lecturing at the university too didn't you?
Yeah. I did some things at the University of Virginia and...
When was the first time you actually presented one of those? I heard a tape a long time
ago of you giving a lecture-demonstration on the history of the saxophone.
Had there ever been another context that you did something like that in before the University of Virginia came along?

No. I thought of it because I had to do one class in the big auditorium, Cabel Hall, for like 350. And then I had to do a workshop type tying in another hour. And this fella, George Starks, who was assistant music director at the university, he plays a little saxophone and what not and he found out I was in town, see, so he says, 'Why don't you come on over here,' 'cause he just came in. So that's how that happened. It was very successful and I started with the history of the saxophone and the different styles, you know, starting with Coleman Hawkins, from 1921 and then came on up to John Coltrane, you know. And the college students they were crazy about Coltrane and

he wrote a tune for me called 'Big Nick' and that seemed to bring me out of the woodwork a little bit, because the college students they were very fond of John Coltrane and they wrote several books on his life and I was in the books. So they were curious about me, you know what I mean. So that's how that got started, you know. So I did all these things for the children, which was a very rewarding experience for me, because children are so innocent and so lovely, you know what I mean. They'd really give me a lift, 'cause in a small community, you know, you have to keep yourself busy, you know, especially if you're from New York. It's like a cultural shock to you. Now I won't pursue that statement, but you know what I mean. (laughter)
